fields.description: The opaque docname series. Nothing about the place, the work or the year goes in the primary key.
fields.label: Series

fields.description: The specification this deployment is run against: what the work is, what a volunteer needs to hold to be a candidate for it, and where it may be used. Configuration a society writes, so that a deployment is an instance of something rather than a description typed out again each time.
fields.label: Terms of Reference

fields.description: ACC-02. Where this deployment sits in the organisational tree, and the field core's geo scoping reads to decide who may see it. A Link, never free text, and mandatory at creation: an unplaced deployment is invisible to geo scoping, because core's list filter is an IN and that excludes NULL. Which level it may sit at is society configuration (ACC-03, vmms_deployment_anchor_level), never a constant, and it must also fall inside the terms of reference's own geo scope where the society has set one.
fields.label: Geo Node

fields.description: Where this deployment is in its life. A closed, code owned set with a fixed transition table in deployment/services/deployment.py, for the same reason approval states are code: each value means something the server enforces, so a society adding an eighth would produce a deployment nothing knows how to handle. Planned is a deployment that has been arranged; Active is one under way; Completed is one that has finished; Cancelled is one that was called off. Note what this does not govern: a time log is accepted on the strength of the roster, not of the status, so a volunteer can still file the hours they served on a deployment that has since completed.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: How many volunteers this deployment needs. The cap the roster is measured against: once that many assignments are Assigned or Accepted, deployment/services/assignment.py::assert_room refuses another, taking a row lock on this deployment first so two coordinators accepting the last place at the same moment cannot both get it. Zero means the society has not said, and a deployment that has not said how many it needs is never full.
fields.label: Volunteers Required

fields.description: The society's own wording for the message a volunteer receives when they are asked to join this deployment. Optional: without one, the notification carries this app's plain sentence. A Link to Frappe's own Email Template rather than a field of prose here, because the wording is a society's and belongs where a society already edits its wording.
fields.label: Email Template

fields.description: The first day of the deployment. Also the date matching asks its questions about when this deployment's own candidate list is built, so a volunteer whose certification expires before the deployment begins is not a candidate for it.
fields.label: Start Date

fields.description: The last day of the deployment. Never earlier than the start date. A deployment of one day has the same date in both fields, which is ordinary rather than a mistake.
fields.label: End Date

fields.description: Superseded by VMMS Deployment Assignment, and retained only so that vmmsx.patches.migrate_participants_to_assignments can read what a site already holds. Nothing writes it. The roster became a register of documents because each person's deployment needed a URL they could open, a reference a notification could point at, a lifecycle with a grammar, and somewhere to record which submitted terms of reference they agreed to — none of which a child row can carry. See deployment/services/assignment.py for the argument in full.
fields.label: Roster (superseded)

fields.description: What has happened on this deployment, in order: notes from the field, milestones, concerns, and the entries the service writes itself when the deployment moves status or somebody joins or leaves. Written only through deployment/services/feed.py, which stamps the author and the time from the session — a feed people could back-date or attribute to somebody else would be worse than no feed. The volunteers' own task reports are not copied in here; api/deployment.py::get_deployment_feed merges them at read time from the tasks linked to this deployment, so there is one copy of each report and it stays with the task it belongs to.
fields.label: Updates

fields.description: Anything the coordinator needs to record about this deployment that is not a field.
fields.label: Notes
